explanation: Unlike in parts of Asia or the Middle East, there is no cultural or religious taboo around feet or their soles in the Netherlands. Propping your feet on furniture or pointing them at someone can still come across as careless or overly casual in someone's home or a formal setting, simply as ordinary manners rather than a deep cultural offense.
local_tip: Keep your feet off furniture and avoid resting them near someone's face, especially in someone's home or a formal setting.

also_check.note: Feet are considered the lowest and most unclean part of the body, so pointing them at people or sacred objects is a serious offense.
Showing the sole of your foot to someone is highly disrespectful, as it implies they are beneath you.
Putting feet on furniture or pointing soles at others is seen as overly casual or rude in more formal settings, similar to the Netherlands.

sources.title: Are there any cultural do's and don'ts in the Netherlands?
